concepts.name: Pelagic Observatory
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE polished desktop software interface concept, wide landscape 16:10, edge-to-edge UI screenshot, no computer hardware or surrounding room. Title ANIMAL ATLAS, small subtitle CONCEPT 01 — PELAGIC OBSERVATORY. This is an animal-activity-driven generative musical instrument, not a tracking admin dashboard. Art direction: exacting flat scientific cartography, midnight navy ocean, subdued blue-grey land, hairline bathymetric contours, warm ivory type, tiny coral and seafoam accents. Rendering technique: razor-sharp 2D vector-like chart graphics and restrained data visualization, NO 3D, no glass, no card grid. Composition: a huge rectangular Pacific-centered world map takes 75% of the screen, New Zealand prominent toward lower middle; fixed narrow right scientific event inspector; one long music/timeline rail along the bottom. Station detections are distinct fixed hollow circles, satellite fixes are tiny diamonds; a few measured shark track segments, no trails between bird stations. Subtle expanding event rings. Right inspector selected 'Tui', 'Acoustic detection', 'BirdWeather', observation time and 'Station location'. Bottom rail shows LIVE ARRIVALS / REPLAY, record control, 60x speed, real timeline strip and four simple performance controls Density, Tone, Decay, Space. Top small source freshness readout distinguishes birds fresh and shark last fix 3 days ago. Use few highly legible labels, large readable typography, compelling professional atlas with quiet musical control. Small footer 'Illustrative data · Design concept'. The overall feeling is a high-end oceanographic observatory translated into a musical instrument. Full coherent interface, not moodboard or multi-panel concept sheet.

concepts.name: Field Notes
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE complete desktop software UI concept in wide landscape 16:10, full-bleed software screenshot, no laptop mockup. ANIMAL ATLAS — CONCEPT 02: FIELD NOTES. Animal events compose music and can be collected and replayed. Entirely distinctive art direction: warm naturalist's field journal meets contemporary editorial publication. Cream handmade-paper surface, faint real paper grain, olive ink, oxblood accent and graphite, beautiful large serif headings with tidy small sans labels, graceful printed rules. Rendering technique: tactile risograph/letterpress cartography with delicate hand-drawn coastline and engraved small bird, whale and shark illustrations, NOT photorealistic wildlife and not childish. Layout unlike a dashboard: asymmetric open-spread composition; the left two-thirds is a large pale world map, with New Zealand in a circular inset and three numbered actual-observation markers; right third is a tall editorial observation journal with generous whitespace, a featured species engraving, selected record 'Tui / acoustic detection / station location / BirdWeather' and an event log with timestamps. Along the bottom a broad printed music staff with discrete event marks doubles as replay scrubber; physical-looking but restrained brass sliders for Density and Decay are integrated into the page margin. Clear Record, Play, observation-time/arrival-time and 60x controls, plus live versus archive label. No black background, no neon, no glass, no modular rack. Useful modern software affordances throughout, sophisticated calm and intimate, a map-based instrument you want to spend hours with. Small 'Illustrative data · Design concept' footer. Crisp readable type, not excessive microtext. One unified screen.

concepts.name: Orbital Biosphere

This is an aspirational aesthetic exploration, with clear functional controls and easy-to-find source attribution. No paper textures, no beige, no flat side-card dashboard, no video game HUD clutter. Footer 'Illustrative data · Design concept'. Single coherent screen.

concepts.name: Biopatch
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE high fidelity desktop UI design for ANIMAL ATLAS, subtitle CONCEPT 04 — BIOPATCH. Wide 16:10 software screenshot, no monitor, desk or background. This concept is a genuinely distinct modular synthesizer instrument layout. Design: light warm-grey anodized aluminium, nearly-black silkscreen type, huge functional orange and cobalt controls, thin orange and blue patch cables connecting modules, precise industrial 2D/2.5D rendered tactile panel, premium restrained hardware material rendering. Layout: left THIRD is a tall MAP SOURCE module containing a meaningful clear flat Pacific-centered world map including New Zealand, live activity markers and source selectors BirdWeather and NZ Sharks; middle THIRD is a PATCH MATRIX with source rows Species, Location, Time, Movement and musical output columns Pitch, Voice, Pan, Decay, visible deliberate few cable connections; right THIRD is a VOICE + SPACE panel with original minimalist waveform, envelope curves, large knobs and output meter. A full-width bottom TAPE module provides recording timeline, observed/arrival mode, Play, Loop, 60x acceleration and recorded event count. Every panel reads as part of one instrument rather than generic floating cards. A little source event strip says 'Tui · Acoustic detection · Station location · BirdWeather'; shark movement mapping visibly available only to actual track fixes, not stationary birds. Friendly precise typography, tactile switches, beautiful negative space. No globe, no dark futuristic glass, no paper journal. Emphasize playability and editable data-to-sound mapping. Small text 'Illustrative data · Design concept'. It must look like a usable ambitious software instrument, not a photo of a physical product.

concepts.name: Living Diorama
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. ONE distinct desktop application concept in wide 16:10, full UI screenshot with no outer device or room. ANIMAL ATLAS, subtitle CONCEPT 05 — LIVING DIORAMA. Direction: contemporary natural-history museum interactive exhibit, playful adult sophistication. Rich forest-green surroundings, warm peach, butter yellow, sea-glass green, chunky expressive typography and clearly delineated real software controls. Rendering technique: beautiful cut-paper layered relief / clay-like stylized 3D illustrated map, visible layered coastlines and soft contact shadows, sculpted materials. Main central surface is a LARGE understandable geographic Pacific map with New Zealand and Australia, layered ocean depth and land, little abstract animal silhouettes at actual illustrative event locations; ecological story without a fabricated bird path. Layout: a bottom 'specimen drawer' holds horizontally arranged source/species selections with tiny embossed bird, shark, whale and turtle silhouettes, making source choice tangible. Four broad vertical performance faders, Density, Motion, Texture, Space, stand on the far-right edge like a tactile exhibit controller. Include a subtle timeline with clear time labels and bookmarks, fresh bird detections versus old shark fixes distinguishable. Generous spacing, fewer controls than a studio rack, approachable for non-musicians but still a real instrument. concepts.name: Migration Score
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE sophisticated complete desktop software interface in wide landscape 16:10, full-bleed screenshot, no device mockup. ANIMAL ATLAS — CONCEPT 06: MIGRATION SCORE. Radical minimalist composition-first art direction: Swiss typography meets experimental graphic music score. Stark white background, near-black ultra-clean line work, one strong vermilion red accent; no gradients, no shadows, no textures, no cards, no hardware skeuomorphism. Rendering technique is high precision flat vector graphic notation and editorial typography. Unusual layout: top 35% is a large extremely spare Pacific-centered geographical map with recognizable continent outlines and New Zealand, thin measured individual track and clearly separate stationary bird station marks; the map is tightly coordinated to a large BOTTOM two-thirds horizontal event score spanning the screen. Score lanes labelled BIRDS, SHARKS, WHALES represent actual source/event classes, showing discrete dots, short stems and sparse gestures as an editable frozen timeline, NOT audio waveforms. A bold red vertical playhead connects the map observation to its place in the score. Narrow right margin contains a concise selected-event receipt 'Tui / Station detection / BirdWeather / Observed 17:04', and four elegant small line sliders Density, Register, Decay, Space. Top typography large ANIMAL ATLAS, restrained transport controls Play / Record / Loop, OBServation vs ARRIVAL time and 60x easy to read. Plenty of negative space, beautiful alignment, map remains substantial and musically useful. No fake data volume claims, no routes connecting unrelated stations. The result should resemble a serious contemporary composition tool and a beautiful printed music score, very unlike a standard map dashboard. Footer 'Illustrative data · Design concept'. One screen only.
